title: No bridge from records or ticks to a clock with a rate
plain: The axioms say records form and stay, and nothing else about time. They do not say how fast, in what order, or how counting events becomes elapsed time. Every lane supplies its own clock. The natural identification, one tick equals one lattice step equals one unit of time, is a naming convention. Different clocks on the same rule give different physics, so the framework cannot yet say what "t" is.

title: The axioms' Z^3 gives a 2D-skewed spacetime or an excluded 3+1
plain: Records sit once on a 3D grid. If that grid is itself space plus time, only two dimensions are space, and the law comes out one-way and lopsided. To get three space dimensions plus time you must let records form again at every tick, which the axioms exclude, or add motion and waves from outside. The good results (long memory, an inverse-distance kernel) live on the excluded version.

title: A propagation cone does not come from records, odds or one-qubit ticks
plain: A light cone needs signals that travel at a finite speed. Odds-based rules (non-negative weights) can only spread out or slide rigidly; they cannot carry undamped waves. Simple one-qubit-per-site quantum ticks are either frozen or move at the top speed with no mass-like curvature. "Nearest neighbour" bounds how far a change could reach only once someone supplies an update rule.

title: Exactly one time (d_t <= 1) is a declared premise; the derivation routes tried are closed
plain: Nothing in the axioms says there is one clock rather than two independent ones. Two commuting clocks fit the axioms. Routes to exclude them either assume the answer, or cannot tell which lattice axis is time, because swapping time with a space axis is an exact symmetry of the staggered hop operator. The result is stated only conditional on a declared premise, B-AXIS.

title: An odd number of time dimensions rests on borrowed anomaly physics
plain: One argument says the number of time dimensions must be odd: a handed (chiral) particle needs an even total number of dimensions, and space is three. But it also assumes the standard anomaly rule, the Standard Model's charges and right-handed partners, none derived here. It yields 1, 3, 5, ..., not 1.

title: One speed for every field is a registered primitive, not a derivation
plain: Space and time could be stretched differently on the lattice, so different fields could travel at different speeds. The framework fixes this by adopting, as an approved building block, that one tick equals one edge in form. Every attempt to derive that from the other axioms is circular or fails. The gravity member is not covered by the block, and on the campaign's continuous-time surface its speed is a free number.

title: One cone is not protected under interactions on the campaign's own time
plain: Even if two fields start at the same speed, interactions shift each one's speed by a different amount, and the shift does not vanish as the lattice is refined. Experiments limit such differences to about one part in 10^15 or better (an external figure quoted in the probe note). A symmetry can prevent it, but the symmetry that works is not the one the campaign's dynamics uses.

title: The Euclidean tick that protects the cone is not the real-time step of the dynamics
plain: The symmetry that protects the cone is a statement about a Euclidean lattice with four equal directions. The framework's dynamics runs in real time. The continuation between the two is proved only for small free systems, and at finite spacing they give different energies. Choosing one changes a headline number (the hierarchy exponent, 16 versus 8), and the tick that keeps a cone cannot carry a one-handed particle.

title: "Time is the creation of records" has no bridge to a clock and clashes with a unitary wave
plain: The owner's picture is that time is records being created or shifted. But if records ride on a unitary quantum wave with Born statistics, the record count cannot rise: records cannot form from nothing. And if a local clock rate is set by record events, Einstein's negative scalar mode either stays or an extra scalar graviton appears; closing it needs an indefinite kinetic form.

title: The arrow of time needs a low-record start
plain: Record formation gives time its direction: away from a start with few records. Why the world began with few records is not derived. The one reduction achieved holds only if records form a single chain, and it leaves the thermodynamic question (why so little entropy) untouched.

title: Three space dimensions are an axiom, not an output
plain: Why space has three dimensions is answered by the first axiom, not derived. The repository's attempt to select three from physics (attraction, stable orbits) works only among a short list of dimensions (1 to 5) and leans on imported physics criteria. Other results (the photon question, the generation count) lean on the number three.
